title: Finding a place to study
goal: Describir un espacio y localizar recursos para una necesidad concreta.
strategy: Antes de leer, imaginá qué necesita una persona para estudiar. Luego separá lo que existe (there is/are) de lo que una persona tiene (has).
passage: There is a new reading room near the station. There are twelve desks, but there aren’t any computers. There is a quiet area upstairs and a small café on the ground floor. The café has an old piano. There are some books in English near the window. Is there a printer? Yes, there is, but it isn’t free. A student asks for an umbrella at reception: it is raining outside.
questions: Can you use a computer there?
El texto dice explícitamente que no hay computadoras. Los doce elementos son escritorios.
Why does a student need an umbrella?
La última oración conecta el paraguas con la lluvia: “it is raining outside”. La información sobre la impresora y el piano no explica esa necesidad.
task: Describí un lugar donde estudiarías. Escribí 60–80 palabras e incluí algo que hay, algo que no hay y una pregunta para recepción.
model: There is a small library near my home. There are six tables and some comfortable chairs. There isn’t a café, but there is a water dispenser. The quiet room is upstairs. There are books in English on the first shelf. Is there a printer for students? I need to print an article for my class. The library is a good place to read.
checklist: Usé is para singular y are para plural.
Elegí a/an según el sonido que sigue.
No confundí there is con have.
contrast: Para expresar existencia, usá there is/are, no have.
